about: Facts behind the cards-c study cards (Italy and Spain, California Cabernet and Napa, Other reds, Dessert and fortified, and the four 1946 Birth Year bottles) of the wine deep dive: each bottle as the Binwise list prints it (catalogue entry n, bin, vintage, size and printed price, the price written with its dollar sign as the cards cite it), and each fact a card states that the guide and the paste do not, with how it is known. Trade knowledge marked certain is general, settled knowledge of the producer or appellation; a fact found by search names where. Nothing here is a score, a vintage report or a quotation. Under mentions, the other bottles of the list the cards name as a step or a mix-up, each as the catalogue holds it, the price with its dollar sign.

bottles.name: Château Latour Pauillac 1er Cru Classé
bottles.card: Château Latour Pauillac Premier Cru Classé 1946

facts.fact: Château Latour is in Pauillac on the Left Bank of Bordeaux, its vineyard (l’Enclos) around a tower near the Gironde estuary; it was ranked one of the first growths (Premier Cru Classé) in the 1855 classification; it is owned by François Pinault (since 1993); the wine is Cabernet Sauvignon led with Merlot.

Brennan’s opened in 1946; the Binwise list files four 1946 bottles under Selections from our Birth Year: Château Latour (bin 27340, $4100), Château Trotanoy (bin 27345, $3700), Château-Figeac (bin 27362, $3200) and Château Canon (bin 27346, $3100).
Château Latour 1er Cru Classé 1946 is also printed in the Pauillac pages at bin 27340 and $4100 (catalogue entry 2249).
Château Latour à Pomerol is a different estate; Beaulieu Vineyard prints a Georges de Latour Private Reserve on the list.

Very old wine: each bottle varies with its storage and cork; it is stood upright, opened with a two-prong (ah-so) opener when the cork is fragile, and decanted only to leave the sediment just before serving; a Coravin needle is not used through an old cork.

Château Trotanoy is a small estate in Pomerol on the Right Bank of Bordeaux, owned by the Moueix family (Établissements Jean-Pierre Moueix, Libourne); the wine is mostly Merlot with Cabernet Franc; Pomerol has no official classification.
Christian Moueix of the same family created Dominus Estate in Napa (Yountville).
Château Trotanoy 1946 is also printed in the Bordeaux pages at bin 27345 and $3700 (catalogue entry 2398).

bottles.name: Château-Figeac Saint-Émilion 1er Grand Cru Classé B
bottles.card: Château-Figeac Saint-Émilion Premier Grand Cru Classé 1946

facts.fact: Château-Figeac is in Saint-Émilion on the Right Bank, on gravel soils beside Château Cheval Blanc near the Pomerol border; it grows a large share of Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc with Merlot, unusual in Saint-Émilion; it was long run by the Manoncourt family.

In the 2022 Saint-Émilion classification Château-Figeac was raised to Premier Grand Cru Classé A; the Binwise list prints Premier Grand Cru Classé B. The first Saint-Émilion classification was made in 1955.
Château Figeac 1946 is also printed in the Saint-Émilion pages at bin 27362 and $3200 (catalogue entry 2421).

bottles.name: Château Canon Saint-Émilion 1er Grand Cru Classé B
bottles.card: Château Canon Saint-Émilion Premier Grand Cru Classé 1946

facts.fact: Château Canon is in Saint-Émilion on the limestone plateau at the edge of the town; it has been owned by the Wertheimer family (owners of Chanel) since 1996; the wine is Merlot with Cabernet Franc. Château Canon-la-Gaffelière is a different estate.
Château Canon 1946 is also printed in the Saint-Émilion pages at bin 27346 and $3100 (catalogue entry 2408); the list also prints Canon 2001 at $700 (bin 26343) and 2006 at $380 (bin 26112).

bottles.name: Lopez de Heredia "Cubillo" Crianza
bottles.card: López de Heredia ‘Viña Cubillo’ Rioja Crianza 2016

facts.fact: R. López de Heredia is in Haro, Rioja Alta; founded in 1877 and among the three oldest bodegas in Rioja; family run. Viña Cubillo Crianza is about 70 percent Tempranillo with Garnacha, Graciano and Mazuelo from old vines, hand harvested, fermented in old wooden vats, aged about three years in old American oak barrels made in the bodega’s own cooperage. Viña Tondonia is the house’s older red label.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, klwines.com and flatiron-wines.com product notes on Viña Cubillo; knowledge

facts.fact: Fattoria di Fèlsina is at Castelnuovo Berardenga, on the southern edge of Chianti Classico northeast of Siena; its Chianti Classico (labelled Berardenga in some markets) is 100 percent Sangiovese, fermented in stainless steel, aged about 12 months in medium-size Slavonian oak casks.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, felsina.it product page and astorwines.com

facts.fact: Chianti Classico is the historic zone of Chianti between Florence and Siena; the straw-covered fiasco belonged to old everyday Chianti.

Produttori del Barbaresco is the cooperative of the village of Barbaresco in the Langhe, Piedmont, of about fifty member grower families; its classic Barbaresco is Nebbiolo blended across members’ vineyards and aged in large oak casks; in the best years it bottles single vineyard Riservas (including Asili, Montefico, Ovello and Rabajà).
The list prints Produttori del Barbaresco Asili, Montefico, Ovello and Rabajà 2019 each at $185 (catalogue entries 3139 to 3142), and the classic as Cantina Produttori Barbaresco 2020 at $95.

CVNE (Compañía Vinícola del Norte de España), pronounced KOO-nay and also labelled Cune, is a historic Rioja house in the railway station quarter (Barrio de la Estación) of Haro, Rioja Alta; Imperial is its Reserva and Gran Reserva label, Tempranillo-led with Graciano and Mazuelo; a Rioja Reserva is aged in oak and bottle before release.
facts.how: knowledge, certain; the exact blend sent to the sommelier

facts.fact: The list prints Bodegas CVNE Gran Reserva 2016 at $205 (bin 145221).

Tenuta San Guido is the Incisa della Rocchetta family estate at Bolgheri on the Tuscan coast, home of Sassicaia; Guidalberto is its second red, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, aged in French and American oak, labelled Toscana IGT.

bottles.name: Fattoria di Fèlsina "Rancia" Chianti Classico Riserva
bottles.card: Fattoria di Fèlsina ‘Rancia’ Chianti Classico Riserva 2019

facts.fact: Rancia is a single vineyard of Fattoria di Fèlsina at Castelnuovo Berardenga, bottled as a Chianti Classico Riserva, 100 percent Sangiovese, aged in oak barrels; a Chianti Classico Riserva has longer aging than the annata.
facts.how: knowledge, certain; felsina.it product pages seen in search 4 October 2026

facts.fact: The list prints Fèlsina Rancia Riserva 2019 (bin 16433) and 2020 (bin 15672), both at $165.

Asili is a celebrated vineyard (cru) in the village of Barbaresco; Produttori del Barbaresco bottles its members’ single vineyards separately in the best vintages, as Riservas, aged in large oak casks.
facts.how: knowledge, certain; the Riserva wording on this bottle sent to the sommelier

facts.fact: Il Poggione is the Franceschi family estate at Sant’Angelo in Colle in the south of Montalcino; its Brunello di Montalcino is 100 percent Sangiovese, aged in large oak casks; Brunello di Montalcino must be Sangiovese only and age years in barrel and bottle before release.

Bin 17832 is printed twice: Il Poggione Brunello di Montalcino 2018 at $198 (entry 3295) and Grgich Hills Napa Valley 2020 at $90 (entry 3089). Il Marroneto Brunello di Montalcino 2019 is on the same page (entry 3293).

bottles.name: Dominio de Pingus "Flor de Pingus" Ribera del Duero
bottles.card: Dominio de Pingus ‘Flor de Pingus’ Ribera del Duero 2022

facts.fact: Dominio de Pingus was created by the Danish winemaker Peter Sisseck at La Horra in Ribera del Duero, Castilla y León; Pingus is made in tiny quantities and Flor de Pingus is the estate’s second wine; both are Tinto Fino (Tempranillo), biodynamically farmed, aged in French oak.

La Rioja Alta S.A. is a historic Rioja house in the railway station quarter of Haro; the Gran Reserva 904 is Tempranillo with a small share of Graciano, aged about four years in American oak barrels made in the house’s own cooperage, then in bottle; a Gran Reserva is Rioja’s longest aged category.
facts.how: knowledge, certain; the exact blend and barrel time for 2015 left to the sommelier

facts.fact: Bartolo Mascarello is a small family cellar in the village of Barolo, run by Maria Teresa Mascarello; its single Barolo is blended from four vineyards in Barolo and La Morra (Cannubi, San Lorenzo, Rué and Rocche dell’Annunziata), with long maceration and aging in large old Slavonian oak casks.
The list prints Bartolo Mascarello Barolo/La Morra in nine vintages: 2011 $260, 2014 $285, 2015 $325, 2016 $850, 2017 $340, 2018 $560, 2019 $420, 2020 $510, 2021 $500.

Gaja is the family winery in the village of Barbaresco, Piedmont; Angelo Gaja made it world famous; its Barbaresco is 100 percent Nebbiolo from the family’s vineyards in the village; Ca’Marcanda (Bolgheri) and Pieve Santa Restituta (Montalcino) are the family’s Tuscan estates.
The list prints Gaja 2012 (bin 16332, $380) on the Piedmont Barbaresco page; Gaja Barbaresco 2020 at $400 appears as a 750ml (entry 89, bin 15481) and as a 375ml half-bottle (entry 3126, bin 15481).

bottles.name: Tenuta Greppo "Biondi Santi" Annata Brunello di Montalcino
bottles.card: Biondi Santi Tenuta Greppo Brunello di Montalcino 2012

facts.fact: Biondi Santi is credited with creating Brunello di Montalcino in the nineteenth century at Tenuta Greppo near Montalcino; in December 2016 the EPI group of the Descours family, which also owns Piper-Heidsieck, Charles Heidsieck and Rare Champagne, acquired the majority of the estate. The annata Brunello is 100 percent Sangiovese aged in large Slavonian oak casks.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, winenews.it (EPI acquisition of the Greppo estate) and tonywooditalianwine.com; knowledge

facts.fact: The list prints Biondi Santi Annata 2012 $425 and 2013 $455, Riserva 1999 $3480, 2011 $1200, 2015 $1430, and Rosso di Montalcino 2019 $255.

bottles.name: Tenuta San Guido "Sassicaia" Bolgheri Sassicaia DOC

facts.fact: Sassicaia is made at Tenuta San Guido, the Incisa della Rocchetta family estate at Bolgheri on the Tuscan coast; it is Cabernet Sauvignon with Cabernet Franc, aged in French oak; it is regarded as the first Super Tuscan; Bolgheri Sassicaia is a DOC of its own, the only one in Italy for a single estate.

Tignanello is made by Marchesi Antinori, a Florentine wine family of many centuries, from the Tignanello vineyard on its Santa Cristina estate in the Chianti Classico hills; it is Sangiovese with Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc aged in small oak barrels, one of the first Super Tuscans, labelled Toscana IGT.
The list prints Marchesi Antinori Solaia Toscana Rosso 1.5L Magnum 2012 at $2230 (bin 29663).

Vega Sicilia is the historic estate at Valbuena de Duero in Ribera del Duero, Castilla y León, owned by the Álvarez family; Único, its flagship, is Tinto Fino (Tempranillo) with Cabernet Sauvignon, aged about ten years in barrels of various sizes and in bottle before release; Valbuena 5° is its younger red, released at about five years.
The list prints Vega Sicilia Único Reserva Especial NV $1040, Valbuena 5° 2013 $420 and 2014 $450.

Masseto is 100 percent Merlot from a single hill of blue clay at Bolgheri on the Tuscan coast, first bottled by Tenuta dell’Ornellaia and since 2019 run as its own estate; both belong to the Frescobaldi family; aged in new French oak. Ornellaia itself is a Bordeaux blend.
The list prints Tenuta Dell’Ornellaia Masseto Toscana Rosso 2011 $1080, 2015 $1225, 2016 $1300 and 2020 $1045.

Chappellet was founded by Donn and Molly Chappellet on Pritchard Hill in the eastern hills of the Napa Valley in 1967; Mountain Cuvée is a Cabernet Sauvignon-led Bordeaux-style blend (2023: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Petit Verdot, Malbec, Cabernet Franc; the blend varies by vintage) from estate and other Napa vineyards.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, chappellet.com technical sheets for 2021 and 2023 Mountain Cuvée, klwines.com

facts.fact: The list prints Chappellet Signature 2022 at $200 and Pritchard Hill 2022 at $705.

Duckhorn Vineyards is in St. Helena, Napa Valley, founded by Dan and Margaret Duckhorn (1976), first known for Merlot (Three Palms); its Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon is Cabernet-led with small amounts of other Bordeaux varieties, aged in French oak.

Duckhorn Napa Valley 2022 at $90, bin 1876, is printed under Selections Under $100 (entry 41) and in the Napa Cabernet pages (entry 2835); a Duckhorn Napa Valley 2022 at $50 (bin 148331) is printed on the Sauvignon Blanc page (entry 1379).

Frog’s Leap is John Williams’s winery in Rutherford, Napa Valley, known for organic farming and dry farming (no irrigation); the Estate Rutherford Cabernet Sauvignon comes from its own Rutherford vineyards. Rutherford is known for a dusty, earthy note in its Cabernet (Rutherford dust).
The list prints Frog’s Leap Estate Rutherford 2020 $200 and 1991 at $410 (Cabernet page) and $300 (Merlot page), and Frog’s Leap Napa Valley 2023 whites at $70 (Sauvignon Blanc) and $95 (Chardonnay).

Caymus Vineyards is the Wagner family winery in Rutherford, Napa Valley, run by Chuck Wagner and family, known for a ripe, plush Cabernet Sauvignon; Special Selection is its top Cabernet from the best lots.

bottles.name: Shafer Vineyards "One Point Five" Napa Valley
bottles.card: Shafer ‘One Point Five’ Stags Leap District Cabernet Sauvignon 2023

facts.fact: Shafer Vineyards is the Shafer family estate in the Stags Leap District on the east side of the Napa Valley; One Point Five Cabernet Sauvignon is named for founder John Shafer and his son Doug (one and a half generations); Hillside Select is its top Cabernet. Stags Leap District Cabernet is known for soft, velvety tannin.
The list prints Shafer One Point Five Cabernet Sauvignon 2021 at $150 on the Half-bottles page (entry 114) and Shafer Hillside Select in vintages from 2005 ($435) to 2022 ($750).
Inglenook is a historic Rutherford estate in the Napa Valley, restored by Francis Ford Coppola and his family; Rubicon is its flagship, a Cabernet Sauvignon based blend.
facts.how: knowledge, certain; the guide describes Rubicon as Inglenook’s flagship

facts.fact: Bin 18231 is printed for the Rubicon 2010 by the glass at $70 (entry 14) and the bottle at $360 (entry 2894); the list also prints Rubicon 2005 $355 and 2009 $360.

bottles.name: Silver Oak Napa Valley
bottles.card: Silver Oak Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2020

facts.fact: Silver Oak Cellars was founded by Justin Meyer and Ray Duncan and is run by the Duncan family; it makes only Cabernet Sauvignon, in Napa Valley and Alexander Valley bottlings, aged only in American oak and rested in bottle before release.
The list prints Silver Oak Alexander Valley 2021 at $180 (bin 148332).

bottles.name: Ridge Vineyards "Monte Bello" Santa Cruz Mountains

facts.fact: Ridge Vineyards makes Monte Bello from its vineyard on a high limestone ridge in the Santa Cruz Mountains, south of San Francisco; it is a Cabernet Sauvignon-led blend with Merlot, Petit Verdot and Cabernet Franc, aged in American oak; Paul Draper was its longtime winemaker. Monte Bello took part in the 1976 Judgment of Paris tasting and placed first at the 2006 rematch.
The list prints Ridge Vineyards Estate Cabernet Sauvignon Santa Cruz Mountains 2020 at $110 (entry 112), Lytton Springs 2022 at $120 and Three Valleys 2023 at $60.

Joseph Phelps Vineyards is in St. Helena, Napa Valley; Insignia, first made with the 1974 vintage, was California’s first proprietary Bordeaux-style blend; it is Cabernet Sauvignon-led with other Bordeaux varieties, aged in new French oak.
The list prints Joseph Phelps Insignia Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley 1.5L Magnum 2015 at $950 (bin 1119).

bottles.name: Caymus Special Selection Napa Valley
bottles.card: Caymus ‘Special Selection’ Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon 2018

facts.fact: Special Selection is Caymus Vineyards’ top Cabernet Sauvignon, made by the Wagner family in some years from its best lots, aged longer in oak than the Napa Valley bottling.
The list prints Caymus "Special Select" Napa Valley 1.5L Magnum 2019 at $950 (bin 11231).

Dominus Estate was created by Christian Moueix (of the Moueix family of Libourne, associated with Pétrus and owners of Trotanoy) on the historic Napanook vineyard at Yountville, Napa Valley; the wine is Cabernet Sauvignon with Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot; Napanook is also the name of its second wine.
The list prints Dominus Estate Napa Valley 2001 at $480 (bin 16148).

Heitz Cellar was founded in St. Helena, Napa Valley, by Joe and Alice Heitz; Martha’s Vineyard in Oakville was planted by Tom and Martha May; Heitz bottled it as a single vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon from the 1966 vintage, among the first vineyard-designated Napa wines; it is known for a mint and eucalyptus note.

Opus One was founded as a partnership of Robert Mondavi and Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Château Mouton Rothschild, with its winery in Oakville, Napa Valley; the wine is a Cabernet Sauvignon-led Bordeaux blend aged in new French oak; Overture is its second wine.

The list prints Opus One 2003 $800, 2005 $900, 2007 $915, 2010 $775; Overture NV $345; a 1.5L magnum 2010 $1550; and, on the Half-bottles page, Opus One Bordeaux Blend 2011 $270, 2014 $305, 2015 $275 and 2016 $280 with no size printed.

Harlan Estate was founded by Bill Harlan in the western hills above Oakville, Napa Valley, aiming at a California first growth; it is a Cabernet Sauvignon-led Bordeaux blend aged in new French oak, made in small quantities and sold mainly by mailing list.

bottles.name: Screaming Eagle "Second Flight" Bordeaux Blend Napa Valley CA

facts.fact: Screaming Eagle is a tiny cult estate in Oakville, Napa Valley, sold mainly through its mailing list; Second Flight, renamed The Flight from the 2015 vintage, is its second wine. Withdrawn by the repairer, 4 October 2026: that it is made in smaller amounts than the estate wine (published figures give about 710 cases of the 2012) and that the 2012 holds more Cabernet than usual; the 2012 is reported as 48 percent Cabernet Sauvignon, 43 percent Merlot and 9 percent Cabernet Franc, which the card leaves to the sommelier.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, klwines.com and vinfolio.com product notes on the 2012 Second Flight; knowledge

facts.fact: Three Valleys is Ridge Vineyards’ Sonoma County blend based on Zinfandel with Petite Sirah and other field grapes from several Sonoma valleys; Ridge also makes Lytton Springs (Dry Creek Valley) and Monte Bello (Santa Cruz Mountains). White Zinfandel is a different, sweet pink style.
facts.how: knowledge, certain; the 2023 blend sent to the sommelier

bottles.name: Ken Wright Cellars Willamette Valley
bottles.card: Ken Wright Cellars Willamette Valley Pinot Noir 2024

facts.fact: Ken Wright Cellars is in Carlton, in Oregon’s Willamette Valley; Ken Wright is known for single vineyard Pinot Noirs; the Willamette Valley Pinot Noir is his blend across vineyard sources.
The list prints Ken Wright Cellars Freedom Hill 2021 $150, Canary Hill Vineyard 2021 $150, Carter Vineyard 375ml 2022 $72, and magnums at $300.

bottles.name: Piedrasassi "Bien Nacido" Santa Maria Valley CA
bottles.card: Piedrasassi ‘Bien Nacido Vineyard’ Santa Maria Valley Syrah 2021

facts.fact: Piedrasassi is the Syrah label of Sashi Moorman and his wife Melissa Sorongon, made in Lompoc, California, since 2003, in a Northern Rhône style; its Bien Nacido Syrah comes from old vines (X block, planted 1973) in Bien Nacido Vineyard, Santa Maria Valley, among the oldest Syrah vines on the Central Coast; Bien Nacido has been described as biodynamically farmed for that block.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, wine.com and fruitwineco.com product notes, skurnik.com producer page

facts.fact: The list prints Piedrasassi Rim Rock Arroyo Grande Valley 2021 at $80 (bin 1627).

bottles.name: Ridge Vineyards "Lytton Springs" Dry Creek Valley

facts.fact: Lytton Springs is Ridge Vineyards’ estate in the Dry Creek Valley, Sonoma County, with old vines planted as a field blend of Zinfandel, Petite Sirah, Carignane and other grapes; the wine is aged in American oak and labelled Lytton Springs, without Zinfandel, when the Zinfandel share is below the labeling threshold.
facts.how: knowledge, certain; the 2022 blend sent to the sommelier

facts.fact: Penfolds is South Australia’s most famous wine house, maker of Grange; its wines carry cellar bin numbers; Bin 389 is a Cabernet Sauvignon and Shiraz blend aged in American oak hogsheads, including some that previously held Grange, and is nicknamed Baby Grange; it is usually labelled South Australia (multi-regional).
facts.how: knowledge, certain; the region printed by the list sent to the sommelier

bottles.name: Kosta Browne Sonoma Coast
bottles.card: Kosta Browne Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir 2021

facts.fact: Kosta Browne was founded in Sebastopol, Sonoma County, by Dan Kosta and Michael Browne, restaurant workers who began with saved tip money; it is known for rich, polished Pinot Noir; the Sonoma Coast bottling is aged in French oak.
The list prints Kosta Browne Sonoma Coast 2020 $240; on the Half-bottles page Kosta Browne Pinot Noir Russian River Valley 2021 $120 and Gap’s Crown Vineyard Sonoma Coast 2014 $165.

bottles.name: Duckhorn "Three Palms" Napa Valley
bottles.card: Duckhorn ‘Three Palms Vineyard’ Napa Valley Merlot 2020

facts.fact: Three Palms Vineyard is on a rocky alluvial fan on the Napa Valley floor near Calistoga, named for three palm trees on the property; Duckhorn Vineyards (St. Helena, founded by Dan and Margaret Duckhorn) made its name with Three Palms Merlot.
The list prints Duckhorn Three Palms Napa Valley 1.5L Magnum 2016 $435 and 3L Double Magnum 2015 $870, and Duckhorn Merlot Napa Valley 2020 $60 on the Half-bottles page.

Château Musar was founded by Gaston Hochar (1930) and made famous by his son Serge Hochar, who kept making wine through the Lebanese civil war; grapes are grown in the Bekaa Valley and the winery is at Ghazir, north of Beirut; the red is Cabernet Sauvignon, Cinsault and Carignan, aged in oak and bottle and released several years after the vintage; its style is individual and savory.
The list prints Chateau Musar Bekaa Valley 1994 $400, 1995 $450, 1997 $285, 2003 $285 and Musar Hochar 2020 $90.

Penfolds Grange was created by Max Schubert, Penfolds’ chief winemaker, in the 1950s after a visit to Bordeaux; it is Shiraz, usually with a small share of Cabernet Sauvignon, blended from old vineyards across South Australia and aged in new American oak; it is usually labelled South Australia.
The list prints Penfolds Grange Shiraz Barossa Valley 2004 $650, 2009 $875, 2010 $875, 2011 $775.

Castello Banfi is a large Montalcino estate founded by the Mariani family, American wine importers; Florus is its late harvest Moscadello di Montalcino from Moscato Bianco, partly oak aged; Moscadello was Montalcino’s historic sweet wine before Brunello.
Castello di Ama and Castello di Volpaia are printed on the same list.

Weingut Hexamer is a family estate at Meddersheim on the Nahe, Germany; Meddersheimer Rheingrafenberg is its best known vineyard; Spätlese is the late harvest Prädikat; a petrol note is typical of aged Riesling.
The list prints Hexamer Meddersheimer Altenberg Kabinett 2023 $60 and Meddersheimer Rheingrafenberg Trocken 2021 $90.

bottles.name: Domaine des Baumard "Clos Sainte Catherine" Coteaux du Layon
bottles.card: Domaine des Baumard ‘Clos Sainte Catherine’ Coteaux du Layon 2006

facts.fact: Domaine des Baumard is a family estate at Rochefort-sur-Loire, Anjou, Loire Valley; the Clos Sainte Catherine is its walled vineyard in the Coteaux du Layon, made as sweet Chenin Blanc; the Coteaux du Layon are slopes along the Layon river known for late-ripened sweet Chenin.

bottles.name: Dr. Hermann "Urziger Wurtzgarten in der Kranklei" Goldkapsel Spätlese
bottles.card: Dr. Hermann ‘Ürziger Würzgarten in der Kranklei’ Riesling Spätlese Goldkapsel 2018

facts.fact: Weingut Dr. Hermann is a family estate at Erden on the Mosel; the Ürziger Würzgarten (spice garden of Ürzig) is a steep red slate vineyard, and in der Kranklei is a parcel within it; Goldkapsel (gold capsule) marks a richer selection within a Prädikat; the list spells it Urziger Wurtzgarten.
The list prints Dr. Hermann Erdener Herzlei Goldkapsel Spätlese 2021 $110 and Erdener Prälat Auslese 375ml 2014 $80.

Domaine Huet is the leading estate of Vouvray in the Touraine, Loire Valley, farmed biodynamically, with three famous vineyards (Le Haut-Lieu, Le Mont, Clos du Bourg); each vintage it makes sec, demi-sec or moelleux wines by vineyard; Chenin Blanc.

Domaine Huet Le Mont Vouvray Moelleux 2009 at $135, bin 33431, is printed on the Loire page (entry 650) and under Dessert Wines (entry 3529); the list also prints Le Mont Demi-Sec 2023 at $105 and as a 375ml half at $60.

Weinlaubenhof Kracher is at Illmitz on the eastern shore of the Neusiedlersee, Burgenland, Austria; Alois Kracher made it famous for sweet wine, and his son Gerhard runs it. The 2017 Cuvée Auslese blends Welschriesling and Chardonnay; the proportion is disputed (one source read gave 60 percent Welschriesling, most published sources give 60 percent Chardonnay and 40 percent Welschriesling), so the card leaves it to the sommelier. It is fermented and matured about 11 months in stainless steel, and is commonly bottled as a 375ml with a screw cap.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, decantalo.com and buzzwines.com product notes, cellartracker.com; knowledge

facts.fact: Bin 19234 is printed for Alois Kracher Auslese 2017 $190 (entry 3544), Calera Viognier Doux Mt. Harlan 375ml 2017 $90 (entry 3532) and Donatella Cinelli Colombini Vin Santo 375ml 2009 $120 (entry 3539).

bottles.name: Château Climens Premier Cru Classé Barsac
bottles.card: Château Climens Barsac Premier Cru Classé 2010

facts.fact: Château Climens is a Premier Cru Classé (first growth) of Barsac in the 1855 classification of Sauternes and Barsac; it makes its sweet wine from Sémillon alone, on limestone, farmed biodynamically, hand picked in successive passes for botrytis (noble rot), aged in oak; Barsac wines may be labelled Barsac or Sauternes.

bottles.name: Inniskillin Cabernet Franc Ice Wine Niagara Penninsula VQA
bottles.card: Inniskillin Cabernet Franc Icewine Niagara Peninsula 2015

facts.fact: Inniskillin was founded by Donald Ziraldo and Karl Kaiser on the Niagara Peninsula of Ontario, Canada, and made Canadian icewine famous; icewine is made from grapes naturally frozen on the vine, picked and pressed while frozen; Inniskillin makes a red icewine from Cabernet Franc; icewine is commonly sold in 375ml or smaller bottles.
facts.how: knowledge, certain; the bottle size sent to the sommelier

bottles.name: Château Suduirant Sauternes
bottles.card: Château Suduiraut Sauternes Premier Cru Classé 2010

facts.fact: Château Suduiraut is a Premier Cru Classé of Sauternes (1855) at Preignac, beside Château d’Yquem, owned by AXA Millésimes; the wine is Sémillon with some Sauvignon Blanc from botrytis-affected grapes, aged in oak; the list spells it Suduirant.
The list prints Château Suduirant Sauternes 375ml Half-bottle 2016 at $135.

Maison Trimbach (F.E. Trimbach) is a family house at Ribeauvillé, Alsace, best known for dry Riesling; Vendanges Tardives is the Alsace late harvest designation; the list files the 2007 under Gewurztraminer (France ~ Alsace ~ White) and spells it Vendages Tardives.
The list prints F.E. Trimbach Vendanges Tardive 2000 at $145 (bin 227520) and Cuvée des Seigneurs de Ribeaupierre 2007 at $305.

bottles.name: Giuseppe Quintarelli Recioto della Valpolicella
bottles.card: Giuseppe Quintarelli Recioto della Valpolicella Classico 1997

facts.fact: Giuseppe Quintarelli was the leading traditionalist of Valpolicella, with his estate in the hills above Negrar near Verona, now run by his family; Recioto della Valpolicella is the sweet red made from Corvina, Corvinone, Rondinella and other local grapes dried for months (appassimento), fermented and stopped while sweet; Amarone is made the same way but fermented dry.

Bin 19321 is printed for Giuseppe Quintarelli Recioto della Valpolicella 1997 $500 (entry 3543) and Taylor Fladgate Quinta de Vargellas 1987 $185 (entry 3576). The list also prints Quintarelli Amarone della Valpolicella Classico 2000 at $925.

Château Gilette is a small estate at Preignac in Sauternes, run by the Médeville family; it ages its Sauternes for many years (often around two decades) in small concrete vats before bottling and release; Crème de Tête is its top selection, Sémillon with some Sauvignon Blanc; it was not classified in 1855.

Château d’Yquem in Sauternes was the only estate ranked Premier Cru Supérieur in the 1855 classification of Sauternes and Barsac; it is owned by LVMH; the wine is Sémillon with Sauvignon Blanc, picked in successive passes berry by berry for botrytis, aged in new oak; it is not made in poor vintages.
The list prints Château d’Yquem Sauternes 1996 $1350, 2001 $1750, 2007 $850, 375ml halves 2015 and 2016 at $450, and a 1500ml magnum 2016 at $1600.

Bodegas Barbadillo is a family sherry house in Sanlúcar de Barrameda at the southwest tip of Spain, known for manzanilla; its Pale Cream is essentially a sweetened fino (some sources say a blend of Palomino with Moscatel), pale gold, apricot, honey and vanilla, bottled at about 17.5 percent; the pale cream style dates from the 1970s.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, dorsetwine.co.uk and harrogatefinewinecompany.com product notes; knowledge

facts.fact: Feist was founded in 1836 in London by two German cousins, H. and C.J. Feist, opened in Oporto in 1870, was taken over by Barros in 1953 and bought by Sogevinus in 2006; it is a small vintage producer, mainly rubies and tawnies, and makes Late Bottled Vintage Port.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, vintageport.se house page on Feist

facts.fact: Port is fortified with grape spirit during fermentation, leaving it sweet; Late Bottled Vintage Port is from a single year and bottled after four to six years in wood.

Sandeman is a historic Port house founded in London by George Sandeman (1790); its emblem is the Don, a caped figure in a wide-brimmed hat; Port is the fortified sweet red of the Douro; a Late Bottled Vintage is from a single year, aged four to six years in wood before bottling.
The list prints Sandeman 1977 at $275 (bin 19311).

bottles.name: Taylor Fladgate "Quinta de Vargellas"
bottles.card: Taylor Fladgate ‘Quinta de Vargellas’ Vintage Port 1987

facts.fact: Quinta de Vargellas is Taylor Fladgate’s estate in the Douro Superior and the backbone of its vintage Ports; in good years not declared as a classic vintage, Taylor bottles it as a single quinta vintage Port; vintage Port is bottled young, ages in bottle and throws a crust; Taylor did not declare a classic vintage in 1987.
The list prints Taylor Fladgate 1977 $580 (bin 19222), 1994 $325 (bin 19122) and Quinta de Vargellas 1987 $185 (bin 19321).

Riveyrac Rivesaltes 1975 (sold as La Cuvée des Aigles) is a vin doux naturel of Grenache and Grenache Gris, fortified by mutage and oxidatively aged for decades in old casks, about 15.5 percent; Riveyrac wines come from the Salses-le-Château cooperative cellar in the Pyrénées-Orientales, founded by eight growers in 1909.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, benchmarkwine.com and bestofwines.com product pages on Riveyrac Rivesaltes 1975

facts.fact: Rivesaltes is a vin doux naturel appellation of Roussillon near Perpignan; Muscat de Rivesaltes is a separate, lighter Muscat appellation. Bin 193312 is printed for Riveyrac Rivesaltes 1975 $190 (entry 3545) and Marco de Bartoli Bukkuram Padre Della Vigna Pantelleria 2008 $200 (entry 3542).

Graham’s is a Port house owned by the Symington family, its home estate Quinta dos Malvedos in the Douro; its vintage Ports are known for a rich, ripe style; vintage Port is made in declared years, bottled after about two years in wood and aged in bottle, where it throws a crust; 2000 was a generally declared vintage.

Bartholomew Broadbent is a British wine merchant and Madeira specialist, founder of Broadbent Selections and a leading importer of Madeira into North America, who bottles Madeira under the Broadbent label; Wine Spectator lists Broadbent Madeiras under Justino’s Madeira Wines. The Broadbent Single Cask Malvasia 2009 (cask N122) is a 500ml bottling aged in old 650 litre oak casks.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, broadbent.com, winespectator.com wine detail pages, ebay.com listing of cask N122; the cask and maker sent to the sommelier

facts.fact: Madeira is a fortified wine of the Portuguese island of Madeira, aged warm, which makes it long-lived and stable once opened; Malvasia (Malmsey) is the sweetest of the grape-named styles. The list prints Broadbent Single Cask Verdelho 500ml 1997 at $270.

Dow’s is a Port house owned by the Symington family, its home estate Quinta do Bomfim in the Douro; its vintage Ports are known for a drier style; 1985 was a declared vintage; vintage Port throws a crust and is decanted.
The list prints Dow’s 1994 $250, 2000 $165 and a 375ml 2000 at $120.

Graham’s, a Symington family Port house with its home estate at Quinta dos Malvedos, declared 1983 as a vintage; vintage Port throws a crust and is decanted; old Port corks may crumble and are drawn with a two-prong opener or the neck broken with port tongs.
Bin 191212 is printed for Graham’s 1948 $1200 (entry 3560) and Graham’s 1983 $265 (entry 3562).
Niepoort is a family Port house of Dutch origin in Porto, led by Dirk Niepoort, also a leading maker of Douro table wines; it is known for elegant Ports and for old Colheitas and Garrafeiras.
The list prints Niepoort Vintage 1980 $435, 1982 $410, 1983 $390, 1987 $305, Colheita 1934 $2650 and Garrafeira 1977 $1500.

Taylor Fladgate is a leading Port house whose declared vintage Ports are among the most prized, built around Quinta de Vargellas; 1977 was a declared vintage; vintage Port is bottled young, ages for decades and throws a crust.

Henriques & Henriques is a historic Madeira house (history dating to 1850); its Founder’s Solera 1894 is described by the producer and its importer as Malvasia, the solera begun in 1894 and closed in 1899, about 20 percent alcohol, sweet, dark amber with gold and green, dried fruit, spice, honey and old wood. The Binwise list prints it as Verdelho.
facts.how: search 4 October 2026, henriquesehenriques.pt (Founder’s Solera 1894), alpenz.com product page, cellartracker.com; catalogue entry 3548

facts.fact: In a solera, wine is drawn from the oldest casks and refreshed with younger wine over time, so the date is when the solera began, not a single harvest; Madeira is fortified and aged warm, which makes it long-lived and stable once opened.
